item.description: Ukraine needs help this winter, says UN goodwill ambassador and actor Nikolaj Coster-Waldau

item.title: Portugal house prices hit new record as October sees 7.5% annual rise
item.description: House prices in Portugal rose 7.5% in October compared with the same period last year. The price per square metre in Lisbon exceeds six thousand euros.

item.title: Schools closed and roads flooded as new wave of severe weather hits Greek islands
item.description: Although the intense weather phenomena eased during the morning hours, emergency services remain on high alert, as further rain and thunderstorms cannot be ruled out during the day.

item.title: Iran says it can reopen Hormuz in two days if US meets conditions
item.description: Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said the timeline shortened from the seven days first proposed in September was “another indication of Iran’s good-faith approach” but that “everything depends” on Washington.

item.title: Prague, Kraków and Istanbul: These are the best European cities for solo travellers
item.description: A new ranking for solo travel has evaluated the most visited European cities by looking at things like accommodation costs and the perception of safety.

item.title: Apple's new CEO faces earnings test as rising chip costs cloud outlook
item.description: Investors want clarity on Christmas sales, rising memory costs and Apple's AI plans as John Ternus prepares to lead his first earnings call since taking over from Tim Cook.

item.title: From Christmas magic to snowy escapes: 10 of Europe’s best winter travel destinations
item.description: Europe has a wealth of diverse destinations to visit during winter, whether you are looking for snowy escapes, coastal breaks or historic journeys.

item.title: Limited school protests resume in some cities in France as holiday ends
item.description: The government has announced measures, including changing the university admissions process, ensuring more teachers and capping the number of pupils per class.

item.title: Argentina courts AI data centres with no regulation and tax breaks
item.description: Argentina’s president, Javier Milei, is courting AI data centre investment in Patagonia, promising light regulation and tax breaks.

item.title: Alarms and card machines at risk as a million UK lines yet to make digital switch
item.description: Businesses face soaring costs and disrupted services if they delay, as Brussels pushes for copper networks to be retired across the EU by 2035.

item.title: Canadian minister stops short of endorsing EU carbon tax as energy alliance deepens
item.description: The Canadian climate Minister's reluctance to openly commit to cooperation with the EU on its climate policy stems from the fact that Ottawa is effectively seeking an exemption from the bloc's carbon border tax, according to a December 2025 internal document seen by Euronews.

item.title: Bolivia declares national emergency over El Niño as drought hits over 78,000 families
item.description: Drought is already affecting more than 78,000 families in seven regions of the country.

item.title: Suspected cyberattack hits supermarket fridges and freezers in Europe
item.description: The incident has affected supermarket in Belgium, Sweden and Ireland, with fridge and freezer temperatures turned up, spoiling hundreds of thousands of euros worth of food.

item.title: Oil slides on Hormuz deal hopes but Trump keeps Iran strikes on the table
item.description: Oil prices fell on Monday morning as talks in Qatar revived hopes of reopening the Strait of Hormuz, but US President Donald Trump kept the threat of fresh strikes alive and Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu reportedly urged him to hit Iran straight after Tuesday's midterm elections.

item.title: Russia resumes attacks on Ukraine's Kherson region after truce ends, Kyiv says
item.description: The ceasefire enabled a humanitarian mission to the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky and for hundreds of stranded citizens to leave.

item.title: Ryanair eyes cost cuts as it faces a €2 billion rise in its fuel bill next year
item.description: One of Europe's biggest airlines saw its first-half profit fall 15% as higher fuel costs and lower fares outweighed passenger growth.

item.title: Prada champions the human touch and not AI slop for their new Christmas campaign
item.description: Prada's new advertising feels like a direct response to those still indulging in a tech that is threatening human creativity and livelihoods. Their ‘Drawing Prada: Animated By Hand’ campaign shows that the "not-made-by-AI" approach has become a major selling point.

item.title: Can the EU’s energy solutions lower your bills? Take our poll
item.description: EU energy ministers want to shield households and businesses from a harsh winter pricing, as the massive geopolitical shock in the Middle East has sent European gas prices surging past a four-year high of €97 per megawatt-hour.

item.title: Dutch MP proposes law banning 'harmful addictive design features' on all digital platforms
item.description: MP Barbara Kathmann tabled a proposal in the Dutch Parliament to end addictive design features such as endless scrolling, autoplay and manipulative algorithms for all online services including social media, gaming, dating apps and streaming platforms.

item.title: Mbappé’s ‘Chinese dictator’ comment: How do Chinese people react?
item.description: Kylian Mbappé has apologised after remarks about a meme depicting him as Chinese leader Mao Zedong sparked backlash in China. At least three Chinese companies have ended brand deals with the football star, while the controversy has drawn a response from China's Foreign Ministry.

item.title: German MPs and ministers warned iPhones have been targeted by spyware
item.description: Those affected have been told to treat their phones as compromised, but it is not yet known who is behind the attack or how many people were hit.

item.title: Paris riots: France investigates after petrol bomb sets officer on fire
item.description: France has opened an attempted murder investigation after petrol bombs were thrown at police during protests over the rising cost of living in Paris.

item.title: Serbia remembers 16 victims of Novi Sad railway station collapse
item.description: Serbia marks two years since the Novi Sad station collapse, as students in power vow justice for the 16 victims and accountability for alleged corruption.

item.title: 'Now, thank God, we have water': Uzbekistan’s tap water reaches 83% of people, but gaps remain
item.description: Uzbekistan has expanded its drinking water network by upgrading treatment facilities and distribution networks, and extending household connections.

item.title: France recalls 7 million condoms across EU over STI and unintended pregnancy concerns
item.description: French authorities have suspended sales and imports of ultra-thin condoms made by a Malaysian manufacturer after an investigation found defects that could increase the risk of breakage, which could lead to sexually transmitted infections and unintended pregnancies.

item.title: What's the EU's plan to cut your energy bill? Ask the Euronews AI chatbot
item.description: EU energy ministers discussed measures to ease winter energy costs as the Strait of Hormuz remains closed, driving energy bills higher. But what do they include? Ask the Euronews AI chatbot.

item.title: Europe seeks Central Asia's critical minerals as producers push for local processing
item.description: At a forum in Tashkent, participants examined technology transfer, financing and transport routes. A recent German-Kazakh industrial roadmap and preliminary financing terms with a French bank illustrate the different stages of cooperation.

item.title: Londoners revive medieval jousting on electric bikes in Halloween spectacle
item.description: Londoners dressed as medieval knights raced into battle on electric bikes at a Halloween jousting event, drawing hundreds of spectators for a quirky modern twist on the medieval sport.

item.title: Poland's president has 'no competence' to appoint judges, says EPP MEP
item.description: Michał Wawrykiewicz. European People's Party MEP, said that Poland's President Karol Nawrocki is "trying to block the restoration of Rule of Law" in his country after tensions over the Poland's Constitutional Tribunal escalated on Friday.

item.title: 'Absolutely no legal basis' for chaotic scenes in Poland's top court, says Polish secretary of state
item.description: Polish Secretary of State Marcin Przydacz speaks to Euronews on the ongoing constitutional crisis in Poland. On Friday, Polish police were dispatched to the tribunal court to defend Prime Minister Tusk's changes to the judiciary.

item.title: Europe doesn't 'care enough' about Ebola outbreak in DR Congo, says Mary Robinson
item.description: Mary Robinson, Ireland’s former president, has called on G20 countries to release the full €3 billion pledged to contain the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, which has claimed 5,000 lives in less than six months.

item.title: One Czech national and four US citizens among Spain train crash dead, officials say
item.description: The accident was Spain's second high-speed train collision this year and raised fresh questions about the country's rail safety, after a crash in the southern region of Andalusia in January killed 46 people.

item.title: Belgium's king considering PM Bart De Wever's resignation after budget talks fail, palace says
item.description: King Philippe said he regrets that no agreement had been reached and that the country cannot afford a prolonged political crisis.

item.title: 'An unprecedented situation': Warsaw wobbles with constitutional crisis
item.description: Good morning. It’s Monday and my name is Angela Skujins. I’ll be holding the newsletter pen until Wednesday when Mared Gwyn once again graces you in your inbox. On today’s agenda: Trouble in Poland, an update from Ukraine, and rekindling EU-UK ties.

item.title: All nine on board Learjet killed in Florida plane crash near Trump's resort home
item.description: The crash occurred near Cresthaven, a neighbourhood in Palm Beach County that is less than 11 kilometres from Trump's resort home Mar-a-Lago.

item.title: Dashcam captures deadly private jet crash in Florida
item.description: Dashcam footage captures a private jet crashing into a Florida neighbourhood and erupting into flames, killing all nine people on board.

item.title: China’s record-breaking clean tech exports could cut CO2 emissions by 8,400 million tonnes - report
item.description: Clean tech is growing "much faster than anyone predicted just a few years ago” as gas prices continue to soar.

item.title: Europe Today: Tusk v Nawrocki: Poland's Constitutional Tribunal crisis explodes
item.description: Poland's President Karol Nawrocki entered the Constitutional Tribunal to demand the return of its suspended conservative chief judge, as Donald Tusk's government seated new judges and riot police clashed with protesters. We hear both sides, plus Ukrainians braces for winter and the Ebola crisis.

item.title: Le Pen condemns Poland's Constitutional Tribunal crisis, Sikorski tells her not to interfere
item.description: The dispute over the composition of Poland's top court has fuelled an open confrontation with President Karol Nawrocki, who attempted to enter the building on Friday night.

item.title: Ukraine and Russia say air raid alert apps hit by cyberattacks after truce ends
item.description: The cyberattacks came as the longest truce of the war, limited to Ukraine's eastern Kherson region, ended on Sunday after Russia refused the offer of an extension, according to Kyiv.

item.title: Binance resumes withdrawals after billions stolen in hack
item.description: Binance said it had seen withdrawals of around $4.7 billion (€4.21bn) on Sunday, after more than $6 billion (€5.38bn) in virtual assets were stolen from the cryptocurrency exchange in a major hack for which the FBI said North Korea was responsible.

item.title: How Europeans can become ‘better grid citizens’ – without cutting their electricity use
item.description: Green technology is allowing more Europeans to take control of their energy bills and help the continent’s outdated grid.

item.title: Harry Potter set-jetting by train: Five magical rail journeys in the UK
item.description: From Platform 9¾ at King’s Cross station in London to the Scottish viaduct crossed by the Hogwarts Express, these real-life locations bring the wizarding world to life. With the first film marking its 25th anniversary this November, here’s where to go for a spellbinding UK getaway by train.

item.title: Trump rallies in Iowa and Kansas in final push as Democratic divisions shake up Michigan
item.description: US President Donald Trump wrapped up his campaign in Iowa and Kansas with a final push to rally support, as Democrats seek to regain control of Congress.

item.title: Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest F1 champion as Max Verstappen wins race
item.description: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli made history and become the youngest Formula 1 world champion. The 20-year-old driver finished third in the Mexico City Grand Prix race behind Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton.

item.title: Initial results show Bulgaria's acting president Yotova wins runoff election
item.description: According to the count by several polling agencies, Yotova received 58% of the vote. If confirmed by official results, she would become Bulgaria’s first elected female head of state.

item.title: Heidi Klum's 2026 Halloween party costume: a giant bloody replica of her own hand
item.description: “I looked at my hand and I thought, ‘Hey, I think I could fit my body in this somehow,’” Klum said of the inspiration for the costume, per the Associated Press.
